newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia issues visa to Magic Johnson - agency.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia issues visa to Magic Johnson - agency.

text.p: Indonesian immigration officials have issued a visa for former U.S. basketball star Earvin "Magic" Johnson to visit Indonesia, the official Antara news agency reported on Saturday.
Johnson, who stunned the sports world in 1991 when he announced he had become infected with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, was denied a visa to enter Indonesia in 1994 because of his illness.

Antara quoted promotors of Johnson's visit as saying the former star would hold a basketball exhibition in Jakarta next week as scheduled and denied an earlier report that immigration officials had not yet decided whether to issue the visa.
It said the visa was issued by Indonesia's consulate in Los Angeles and gave no other details.
Johnson was denied a visa to enter Indonesia in 1994.

The Republika newspaper said earlier on Saturday immigration officials had not decided to allow Johnson into the country. It quoted immigration spokesman Mursanuddin Ghani as saying Indonesia's immigration act stated the government was entitled to reject anybody whose illness could endanger other people.
"We are still consulting other related institutions," Ghani told the paper.
The World Health Organisation has said as many as 500,000 Indonesians might be infected with the virus.
Indonesia has put the number of HIV or AIDS-related deaths at 465, but health workers said that figure only represented reported cases and the real number could be as much as a hundred times greater.
Indonesia has a population of nearly 200 million people, making it the world's fourth most populous nation.
